meta.title: Operation of Infrared Moisture Balance in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To rapidly determine the moisture content of crude drugs, powdered herbs, and plant extracts using infrared radiation heating with simultaneous gravimetric weight measurement for standardization and quality control.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for rapid moisture determination during crude drug procurement, processing, and before long-term storage — supplementary to the pharmacopeial loss on drying method.
procedure: Switch on the infrared moisture balance and allow 15 minutes warm-up time before the first measurement.
Level the instrument using the built-in spirit level and adjusting the levelling feet.
Clean the sample pan with a dry lint-free cloth; place it on the pan holder.
Tare the empty pan by pressing 'Tare' — the display should show 0.00 g and 0.00% moisture.
Set the infrared lamp drying temperature: 105°C for most crude drugs; 60–80°C for essential oil-containing drugs or thermolabile materials.
Select the automatic shut-off mode (recommended): the balance stops when weight change is < 1 mg per minute.
Grind or powder the sample finely to maximize surface area exposure.
Spread 2–3 g of the sample uniformly across the sample pan in a thin, even layer — do not heap in the centre.
Close the lid — the IR lamp activates and the display shows real-time moisture loss percentage.
Wait for the automatic completion signal or until the reading stabilizes.
Record the final moisture content (%) shown on the display.
Open the lid carefully — the pan and sample are very hot.
Use forceps to remove the hot pan; allow to cool before discarding the sample.
Clean the pan immediately with a dry brush.
Record: sample name, initial weight, temperature, method (auto/timed), final moisture % in the logbook.
Compare against IP/WHO/institutional specification limits for the specific crude drug.
precautions: The sample pan becomes extremely hot (>100°C) during operation — always use tongs or forceps to handle.
Do not look directly at the infrared lamp during operation — intense infrared radiation causes eye injury.
Spread sample uniformly — uneven layering causes inconsistent drying and inaccurate results.
Allow the balance to cool between successive determinations — minimum 5 minutes between runs.
Calibrate using a reference standard material (certified moisture reference or sodium tartrate dihydrate) periodically.
Do not use for samples with reactive or corrosive components — they damage the IR lamp and load cell.
The infrared moisture balance gives rapid results but may differ slightly from pharmacopeial LOD values — use IP method for official reporting.
